text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The area of Brcko has exceptional economic and transport significance for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation, speakers said during eighth day of arbitration hearing on disputed town in Rome.
- Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic discusses with U.S. special envoy to Bosnia Richard Sklar planned economic reforms in Bosnia, emphasising importance of privatisation.

- Formation of Bosnian federation army on principle of national corps means that three national armies officially have been created in Bosnia, a decisive step which will lead to country's definitive division, newspaper commentary says.
- Muhamed Sacirbey, Bosnian ambassador to United Nations, says at business council in New York that there are no grounds for perception that investing in Bosnia is extremely risky.
- Moslem-Croat federation's House of Representatives due to meet on January 22. Proposed laws on privatisation, ownership of flats, health care will be on the agenda.
- Last year Bosnia exported goods worth $23 million and imported $523 million in the same period, Bosnia's Bureau for Statistics says.
- President of Moslem-Croat federation and Croat member of Bosnia's collective Presidency, Kresimir Zubak, has retired a number of Croat militia officers, including six generals.

- Mostar regional office of international High Representative, headed by Sir Martin Garrod, met last night with Mostar Mayor Ivan Prskalo and deputy Safet Orucevic. Reason for extraordinary session was unauthorised work by Croats on theatre in central distict.
- A survey conducted by newspaper shows 63 percent of Bosnian population support reorganisation of federation army.
- Iran supports multinational and multicultural Bosnia, says Momamad Taherian, Iranian ambassador to Bosnia.
